newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London dominated by Dow reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London dominated by Dow reshuffle.

text.p: A reshuffle of the companies comprising the Dow Jones industrial average was the main influence on a mixed U.S. stocks trading session in London on Monday, but dealers said profit-taking could pull Wall Street lower later.
"A bit of profit-taking will continue for the short-term," one dealer said. "We expect to see Wall Street a little bit lower to start with, unless we get a surprise from today's figures."
U.S. retail sales figures for February are due at 1330 GMT, with analysts expecting a monthly rise of around 0.6 percent, the same as in January.
Strong figures could raise expectations of a U.S. interest rate rise on March 25. "The market is a little nervous ahead of the figures," the dealer said.
By 1150 GMT, March S&P 500 futures were 0.70 points lower at 803.00, while the March long bond was down 5/32 at 110.
"The main thing has been the switch of the components of the Dow Jones, which has put the dampeners on some companies which are coming out," a dealer said.
Texaco Inc, Bethlehem Steel Corp, Westinghouse Electric Corp and Woolworth Corp are due to leave the blue-chip index.
Texaco was down $1-1/4 at $101-1/2, Bethlehem Steel fell $1/4 to $8-1/2, and Westinghouse fell $3/8 to $18-5/8.
Dealers said the negative impact on Woolworth was blunted by the company's announcement of good fourth-quarter results and a strong outlook after Wall Street closed on Wednesday.
Taking the place of the ousted companies will be Hewlett-Packard Co, Johnson & Johnson, Wal-Mart Stores Inc and Travelers Group Inc.
Hewlett-Packard shares climbed $3/8 to $55 and Johnson and Johnson gained $3/8 to $60.

Elsewhere, General Motors Corp fell $3/8 to $57-3/8 after releasing a financial breakdown of its auto-building operations and its Delphi auto parts unit in preparation for the sale of 20 percent of Delphi.
Other motor shares came off in sympathy, with Ford Motor Co falling $1/4 to $32-1/2 and Chrysler Corp $1/4 weaker at $31-1/8.
